questions.question_text:
A circle has centre $O$ and radius $OA = 15$ cm. Chord $AB = 24$ cm, and $OM \perp AB$ at $M$.
Find $OM$.

options.why: Subtracts the half-chord from the radius, $15 - 12 = 3$, instead of using Pythagoras' theorem.
Gives the half-chord $AM = 24 \div 2 = 12$ instead of the perpendicular distance $OM$.

questions.solution_text:
$AM = 24 \div 2 = 12$ cm (perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord)
In right-angled $\triangle OAM$:
$OM = \sqrt{15^2 - 12^2} = \sqrt{81} = 9$ cm

questions.question_text:
Circles with centres $P$ and $Q$ intersect at $A$ and $B$. The line $PQ$ meets the common chord $AB$ at $M$, with $M$ between $P$ and $Q$.
$AB = 30$ cm and $QM = 20$ cm. Find the radius $QA$ of circle $Q$.

options.why: Adds the perpendicular sides directly, $20 + 15 = 35$, instead of using Pythagoras' theorem.
Subtracts the squares instead of adding them to find the hypotenuse, giving $\sqrt{20^2 - 15^2} \approx 13.23$.

questions.solution_text:
$PQ$ bisects the common chord $AB$ at right angles at $M$.
$AM = 30 \div 2 = 15$ cm
In right-angled $\triangle QAM$:
$QA = \sqrt{20^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{625} = 25$ cm

questions.question_text:
A circle has centre $O$ and radius $OA = 26$ cm. Chord $AB = 48$ cm, and $OM \perp AB$ at $M$.
Find $OM$.

options.why: Subtracts the half-chord from the radius, $26 - 24 = 2$, instead of using Pythagoras' theorem.
Gives the half-chord $AM = 48 \div 2 = 24$ instead of the perpendicular distance $OM$.

questions.solution_text:
$AM = 48 \div 2 = 24$ cm (perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord)
In right-angled $\triangle OAM$:
$OM = \sqrt{26^2 - 24^2} = \sqrt{100} = 10$ cm

questions.solution_text:
In $\triangle OAM$ and $\triangle OBM$:
$\angle OMA = \angle OMB = 90^{\circ}$ (given, $OM \perp AB$)
$OA = OB$ (equal radii)
$OM = OM$ (common)
$\therefore \triangle OAM \equiv \triangle OBM$ (RHS)
$AM = BM$ (matching sides of congruent triangles)
